history.dynasty: Ahom Kingdom (per visitor accounts - specific builder not documented)
history.summary: Bilvesvar is an ancient Shiva shrine in Jorhat district with a holy tank traditionally said to have been built by Rucinath Burgohain (Buragohain was a high office under the Ahom kings). A 2015 TripAdvisor review describes an Ahom-Kingdom-era temple complex on the South Trunk Road (NH-37) about 35 km from Jorhat City, reachable by taxi and state buses. DISTANCE CONFLICT (verify): hotel-aggregator copy (Wanderlog) instead places a 'Bilvesvar Siva Temple' within walking distance of East Jorhat hotels - one of the two claims is wrong. COORDINATE FLAG: no POI-level geocode match found for this temple (it is distinct from Billeswar Devalaya in Nalbari and from Tezpur's Beleswar temple); coordinates below are the Jorhat town reference only and are approximate - verify before mapping.

name: Bilvesvar Shiva Temple
town_description: Jorhat, on the banks of the Bhogdoi river, is Upper Assam's principal commercial city and is often called the tea capital of Assam - it hosts the historic Tocklai Tea Research Institute. From Nimati Ghat just outside the city, ferries cross to Majuli island. Jorhat is well connected by air (Rowriah), rail and NH-37, and serves as the gateway to Upper Assam's Ahom-era temples, satras and tea gardens.

travel.airport: Rowriah Airport (Jorhat) - about 7 km from Jorhat city (verify).
travel.road: On the South Trunk Road (NH-37); reported ~35 km from Jorhat City per a 2015 visitor review - distance conflict with hotel-aggregator listings, verify.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, the cool dry months, is the pleasant window for temple visits in Upper Assam (verify).
